title: cylinder
body:
## cylinder

Creates a native Part::Cylinder whose base circle is centred at origin and which extends height along axis. Choose it for pins, bosses and round bars, and above all as the tool for a round hole in cut. Unlike circle + extrude it needs no separate profile node; the axis may point in any direction.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- radius is half the hole diameter.
- For a through-hole, start the tool below the part and make it longer than the part is thick (the bracket example uses origin z = -1 and height 10 for an 8 mm plate).
- A zero axis vector fails planning with INVALID_AXIS.

Native binding: `Part::Cylinder`. Output kind: `["solid"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | Radius of the circular cross-section, in millimetres (Part::Cylinder Radius). For a drill tool this is half the hole diameter. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true,"maximum":100000}` | `5` |
| `height` | Length of the cylinder from its base circle along axis, in millimetres (Part::Cylinder Height). | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true,"maximum":100000}` | `10` |
| `origin` | World coordinates [x, y, z] of the centre of the cylinder's base circle; the cylinder extends from here by height along axis. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `axis` | World direction [x, y, z] in which the cylinder extends from its base; Schemaxis rotates the native placement so the cylinder's local Z axis points this way. Only the direction matters ([0, 0, 2] equals [0, 0, 1]); a negated vector makes the cylinder grow to the other side of origin. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,1]` |
